prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported concussion. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1304; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On the afternoon of the incident, Driver 1 was stopped in a queue of traffic on a Pasadena, Texas roadway when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 told the responding officer that the vehicle had slowed suddenly and that there was insufficient time to stop. Driver 2 acknowledged responsibility for the impact and did not dispute the sequence of events. Two independent witnesses on the roadside described the collision in the same way, and both said they saw Driver 1 and a Passenger seated in the vehicle before and after the impact. Scene photographs show rear-end damage to Driver 1's vehicle that is consistent with the reported force of the collision, with no obvious prior damage to the vehicle noted at the scene. Driver 1 reported dizziness and a headache and was later evaluated for a possible concussion. Driver 1 is listed as an insured operator on the policy covering the vehicle. The Passenger declined transport and did not report injury at the scene.
